title: FREE 4/5 days Gentleman split (part. 1)
summary: NH walks through a 4-5 day gentleman split (2 upper, 2 lower, optional weekend arm day) he built for an Instagram follower with weak arms, shoulders and mid back, explaining every rep range, superset, rotating set and exercise ordering choice. He also gives a blank template so viewers can fill in their own movement patterns.
claims: He will never write programs on request or sell programs; everything needed to program for yourself is or will be on the channel
Learning to program for yourself is as important a skill as learning to squat and is what takes you furthest in bodybuilding
He made this one exception because the requester was a good case study and wanted a gentleman split, letting him show the concept in practice
The gentleman split is his own vision of a program as close to perfect as possible
The requester's version is skewed to his weak points (arms, shoulders, mid back), overpowering chest, poor triceps insertions and long biceps; most viewers should use the blank template instead
The blank template gives only movement patterns and frequency, no rep ranges, because rep ranges are volume and intensity manipulation left to the lifter
A gentleman split stays in a striking range of 4 to 5 training days: 2 upper, 2 lower, plus an optional arm day
The arm day sits on the weekend and is optional; removing it does not hurt progression on the other four days, but doing it gives better arm gains
For a lifter with weak shoulders, make the vertical press the main lift of the first upper day
Barbell overhead press as strength work should sit between high intensity and high volume: 3-6 sets of 2-5 reps, never superset
A wide set/rep range lets you push intensity on good days (e.g. 3 sets of 2-3) and volume on others; for those unfamiliar with pyramiding, stick to 3-4 sets of 2-5
Supersetting does not hurt progression; it improves it because the time saved is better invested in practicing movements than in splitting sets
He programs optimally and does not design around commercial gym constraints, but tries to make supersets need minimal equipment (e.g. EZ bar for curls, skull crushers and Pendlay rows)
Giant set: EZ bar curls 6-10, skull crushers 8-12, Pendlay rows 6-10 for 3-4 sets

A 3-4 set evolving range beats fixed 4 sets: fixed sets make you repeat weights trying to get the fourth set, the main flaw of most 5x5s; allowing 3 sets lets you experience heavier weights without feeling you failed
If you cannot do weighted pull-ups, rep ranges matter little: do them unweighted for as many reps as possible, ideally keeping reps in the tank
He personally cannot do weighted chin-ups
Cable lateral raises should be done in higher rep ranges like 10-15 so you can actually crank out reps without forcing them
Barbell shrugs respond well to 10-15 reps; superset with lateral raises for a fixed 4 sets
Fixed set counts are fine on low-specificity accessories because progression on them is not critical and does not feed strength work; it is just volume
End-of-day finisher of diamond push-ups, knee raises and calf raises: AMRAP reps and AMRAP sets, leaving when it stops being productive since you never reach zero
Gentleman splits are not for novices, both for frequency reasons and because much manipulation happens within the workout based on recovery and feel
Order exercises by importance: the lower on the list, the less important, because you want to be freshest for key lifts and the last exercises get skipped most
If a muscle is a big weak point, its exercise must be high in the session even if it is a small body part, so you cannot skip it
Squats for a lifter who wants big legs: 3 sets of 4-8 reps on the one heavy squat day
He himself does 1-3 sets of 4-8 on squats because his quads are already massive and not a focus
Back-off set or variation after squats must be a pure knee flexion with a bar on the back (paused, front, SSB squat), not a good morning: 3 sets of 4-8
If squat volume becomes too much, cut the strength work to 1-3 sets rather than lowering intensity on the back-off
Stiff-legged deadlifts put the back parallel to the floor and target the mid back more than the traps; 6-10 reps for 4 sets
Weighted pull-ups are always 4-6 reps; for 4 sets this is deliberate sandbagging because vertical pulls were done the day before and progression is not pushed there
Many people would benefit from doing leg raises unweighted since they are hard enough already
Back hyperextensions: 4 sets of 8-12, never for high intensity, except when used strictly as a deadlift accessory where 3 reps can apply
Rotating sets: listed alternatives that replace each other week to week (e.g. back extensions instead of stiff legs); days look undoable on paper because only one option is done
Rotating alternatives must strain the same body part, or the missing work must appear elsewhere in the week; this is advanced and easy to lose track of
Calf raises should not go into low rep ranges: 10-15 (8-12 also fine), because calves are small and the Achilles tendon is fragile
Neck work at 10-15 reps, which is even a little low for neck
Calves are always programmed last, so skipping the end of sessions gives chicken legs; finishing them is where you build mental fortitude
Benching once a week will not progress the bench; at best you avoid regressing; horizontal pressing needs frequency
For the strong-chested requester, bench only once a week for 3 sets of 4-6 since the chest steals work from the shoulders
Dumbbell overhead press 8-12 for 4 sets superset with French press 6-10 (8-12 or 10-15 also work); never go below 5 reps on French press
Alternate pull-up and chin-up variations 48 hours apart so you are fresher than repeating the same one
Isolation for forearms, calves and neck is ranked low since compounds working most muscles come first, but ignoring isolation leaves you looking terrible
Wrist curls 8-12 (10-15 fine); try styles including standing and finger curls and drop any that hurt the wrist or are felt in the wrist rather than the forearm
Hammer curls after wrist curls at 6-10 for 3 sets so mechanical failure does not limit him; replace with pinwheel curls if shoulders dislike the position
His own shoulders hate the hammer curl position
Rear delt flies 8-12 in whatever position hits rear delts most; if felt in the traps, do Arnold raises instead
Triceps extensions in front of the body without shoulder flexion at 10-15 to avoid isolating lateral and medial heads too much
If calves are trained twice weekly, make one day heavier (6-10) and one higher volume (8-12) to experience progression faster on one
Upper days should look longer on paper than lower days because lower body accumulates far more tonnage and is far more tiring
On upper days mental stamina limits you; on lower days physical stamina runs out first
Deadlifts are mandatory for a bigger back; about 85% of his back thickness came purely from deadlifting
Deadlift: 2-5 reps for 1-3 sets; it is a lift where low frequency and low reps work if intensity is high and form is on point
If deadlift form is shaky stay at 4-5 reps for 2-3 sets and only add weight when confident, not just when you hit the weight
Most people should do a deadlift variation for back-off rather than straight deadlifts because they cannot recover; he can, but is an exception
Deadlift back-offs: 3 sets of 2-5 if same style, or 8-12 with a variation like RDL; do not superset them for someone not used to deadlifts
Paused squats 3 sets of 4-8 superset with pull-ups finish the posterior chain on deadlift day
Rack pulls touch-and-go for 8-12 to emphasize the upper back; with lower reps the first rep becomes the hardest
Snatch-grip shrugs (his Nippard shrugs) 10-15 reps; build up grip width gradually or start light; gives a mid-back stretch you have never felt
Never do deadlifts, deadlift back-offs and rack pulls in one day: rack pulls only if no back-off sets; snatch-grip shrugs can be done either way
The two deadlift-day versions keep similar lumbar stress, one heavier; on bad days pick the shrug version and skip rack pulls
exercises: strength work, no superset; pyramid optional
superset with skull crushers and Pendlay rows
unweighted AMRAP with reps in tank, or weighted 4-6
try styles; stop if wrist hurts
prone, incline or bent; Arnold raise if traps take over
